fields.name: id
fields.authorityReason: Session must have a canonical identity so revocation, rotation, audit and session listing can address one session instance.

fields.name: userId
fields.authorityReason: Session creation and session listing are actor-scoped; the canonical identity model places Session under User in D1-01.

fields.name: deviceId
fields.authorityReason: The authoritative L5/L6 registry requires sessions to bind to devices and requires privacy-safe device references.

fields.name: tokenVersion
fields.authorityReason: The canonical identity/session contract explicitly binds Session to token_version and requires token invalidation on relevant account-security transitions.

fields.name: refreshCredentialHash
fields.authorityReason: Refresh credentials are tied to a session, must rotate, old credentials must become invalid, and raw secrets must never be persisted or logged.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.authorityReason: Session issue and session expiry claims require an assigned expiry and deterministic expiry enforcement.

fields.name: revokedAt
fields.authorityReason: Session revocation must be durable, auditable, idempotent and authoritative over stale credentials/cache.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.authorityReason: Session issuance and lifecycle auditing require a canonical creation timestamp.

fields.name: lastSeenAt
fields.authorityReason: Session listing and security monitoring require a bounded last-observed session timestamp; refresh/heartbeat implementation must prove update semantics.

invariants: Raw access tokens, refresh tokens, passwords and other credential secrets MUST NOT be stored in this entity.
refreshCredentialHash MUST represent only secret-derived material and MUST never be exposed through public/admin DTOs, events, analytics or logs.
A revoked session MUST fail authentication even when a stale cache or stale credential is presented.
A session MUST be attributable to exactly one authoritative user and one privacy-safe device reference for its lifetime.
expiresAt MUST be evaluated authoritatively; expiration cannot be bypassed by cache state.
tokenVersion MUST participate in the token/session invalidation contract and MUST NOT be client-controlled.
Field additions or changes require a new contract revision plus migration evidence before implementation is considered valid.
nonGoals: No client-controlled authorization role or entitlement field.
No provider-specific OAuth secret storage in Session.
No speculative risk score, IP history, geolocation or fingerprint payload until separately contracted.

verificationRequirements.entityPromotion: ENT-SESSION remains PROPOSED until executable schema, persistence, migration, runtime and Evidence Registry evidence exist.
requiredEvidence: migration artifact and applied migration evidence
